question: Does the public Dupon River reconnaissance abstract provide a usable, verified fish checklist for Isabel, Leyte?

sourceReviewed.citation: Monserate, N. F. T. (2019). Reconnaissance Survey of Stream Fishes in Dupon River, Isabel, Leyte, Philippines. Abstract in De La Salle Araneta University 4th Research Congress / 1st International Research Congress Book of Abstracts, PDF p. 61.
sourceReviewed.access: Downloaded and reviewed the full 112-page conference abstract book from the DLSAU host; the Dupon abstract is on PDF page 61. Public indexed results and the downloaded PDF agree on the four-reach survey and aggregate. No full article, underlying species table or supplementary dataset was located in this source review.

reportedScope.waterbody: Dupon River, Isabel, Leyte; source says it is part of the Dupon, Matlang and Merida Water Quality Management Area.
reportedScope.samplingDesign: Four sites/reaches: estuary, downstream, midstream and upstream. No site coordinates, reach labels beyond those categories, collection dates, sampling gear, effort, or specimen/voucher identifiers appear in the abstract.
reportedScope.reportedAggregate: 13 fish species in 11 families, from total fish catch; family representation highest for ‘Eliotridae’ and Mugilidae as printed. The abstract reports lower richness at estuary and midstream and higher diversity at downstream/upstream, but gives no site-by-taxon table or numerical counts by reach.
reportedScope.verbatimTaxonAnomaly: The abstract text reads ‘Ambacis miops’ and assigns it to ‘Centropomidae’; it calls this the most abundant species at 53.65% of the total catch. Preserve this source string verbatim. It is not silently corrected to Ambassis miops, Ambassis mops, or another species.

taxonomyAssessment.authorityCrosscheck: Eschmeyer's Catalog lists Ambassis miops Günther, 1872 as a valid species in Ambassidae with a broad Indo-West Pacific distribution that includes the Philippines; its genus results also treat Ambassis as valid in Ambassidae and Ambasis as an unjustified emendation. The catalog makes Ambassis miops a plausible intended spelling, but does not authenticate this survey's specimen or establish the local family assignment.
taxonomyAssessment.decision: Preserve the printed ‘Ambacis miops’ and ‘Centropomidae’ verbatim as source text. Record Ambassis miops only as a plausible taxonomic cross-check, not as a corrected survey identification or occurrence; require the full paper, author confirmation, or voucher evidence before resolving it. Preserve ‘Eliotridae’ as printed rather than silently normalizing it to Eleotridae.

crossSourceAssessment.freshwaterScope: Although titled a stream-fish survey, the abstract explicitly includes an estuary and downstream river reaches. Do not label its 13-taxon aggregate as a freshwater-only checklist or assume all taxa were collected in freshwater reaches.
crossSourceAssessment.independence: No crosswalk was found to the Samar SINP, Ormoc Lake Danao/Tubod/Inawasan, or other Leyte river studies. Keep Dupon River as a distinct waterbody lead and do not combine its aggregate with other Leyte surveys.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Research lead only. The abstract does not expose a taxon list, dates, effort, station-to-taxon mapping, voucher catalog, current occupancy, or item-specific reuse terms. It does not establish diet, catchability, safety, legal access, or a usable geometry.

rightsReview.status: The proceedings PDF was publicly downloadable, but no item-specific open license or permission to publish derivative structured records was identified.
rightsReview.handling: No proceedings pages, images, tables, fish data, or copied PDF were added to the repository. Only citation metadata and a short factual summary are retained.

disposition.reason: Only a conference abstract is available in the reviewed source. It lacks the 13-name checklist and specimen/station crosswalk, includes an estuary, and contains an unresolved species/family spelling anomaly.

nextActions: Seek the full Dupon River article, likely associated with Visayas State University-Isabel, and request its exact publication citation, field dates, methods/gear, full 13-taxon list, reach-by-taxon counts, photographs/vouchers and reuse terms; do not send an inquiry without explicit authorization.

Ask the author to confirm whether the abstract's ‘Ambacis miops’ was intended to identify Ambassis miops or another taxon, and reconcile the Centropomidae attribution against the voucher and diagnostic characters.

Keep estuary and freshwater reaches separate if a station-level source is obtained; continue the Eastern Visayas freshwater sweep without counting the 13-species aggregate as verified inventory coverage.

sources.supports: Full conference abstract book, PDF page 61: Dupon River, Isabel, Leyte; four reaches including estuary; aggregate of 13 fish species and 11 families; verbatim ‘Ambacis miops’ / ‘Centropomidae’ string; no checklist or date/gear/voucher table.

Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes species record, updated 7 July 2026: Ambassis miops Günther, 1872 is a valid species in Ambassidae, with a broad range including the Philippines. This only makes the abstract's misspelled string a plausible candidate; it does not verify the surveyed specimens.

Eschmeyer's Catalog family results list Ambassis as valid in Ambassidae and describe Ambasis as an unjustified emendation; used only for nomenclatural context, not to verify the survey identification.
